Mark Drakeford announced he would stand down as First Minister in December 2023, triggering a leadership contest within Welsh Labour [d68245236s1p0].
Vaughan Gething won the ensuing leadership election but his government collapsed in July 2024 amid scandals including allegations of cronyism and that he lied about deleting COVID-19 related text messages [d68245236s1p0].
Gething subsequently announced he would stand down and a later leadership contest was uncontested with Eluned Morgan being elected in July 2024 [d68245236s1p0].
Eluned Morgan failed to retain her seat in the 2026 Senedd election and resigned on 8 May 2026, prompting another leadership election and resulting in Ken Skates being appointed interim leader [d83134346s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What electoral or structural constraints (e.g., voting system, demographic shifts) threaten Welsh Labour's dominance?
sub_answers.text:
Electoral reforms ahead of the 2026 Senedd election increased the Senedd from 60 to 96 members and adopted party-list proportional representation while reducing the number of constituencies to sixteen, altering the electoral system in Wales [d68245236s0p0].
Those reforms coincided with Welsh Labour losing government and dropping to a historic low of nine seats in 2026, ending its long winning streak and reducing its dominance [d68245236s0p0].
Plaid Cymru and Reform UK made significant gains in 2026, with Plaid becoming the largest party and Reform taking second place, demonstrating demographic or political shifts that threaten Labour's prior dominance [d68245236s0p0].
Local election dynamics previously showed substantial seats for independents and gains by Plaid Cymru, indicating competitive pressures at grassroots level that constrain Labour's control [d68713648s1p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How are Welsh Labour candidates for UK Parliament and the Senedd selected under party rules?
sub_answers.text: Leadership candidates need nominations from either 20 percent of the party’s Senedd group, ten percent of Labour MSs and 20 percent of Constituency Labour Parties, or ten percent of MSs plus three nominations from Welsh Labour affiliated organisations including at least two affiliated trade unions.[d83134346s1p0] The text specifies these nomination thresholds for the leader of Welsh Labour, who must be a Senedd member.[d83134346s1p0]

sub_answers.sub_question: How has devolution (creation of the Senedd) altered Welsh Labour's internal decision-making and policy processes?
sub_answers.text: The creation of the Senedd resulted in Welsh Labour leaders being required to be members of the Senedd, tying party leadership to devolved legislative representation.[d83134346s1p0] Welsh Labour has operated as the governing or opposition party within the Senedd system since devolution began in 1999.[d68245236s0p0] Welsh Labour engaged in a formal co-operation agreement with Plaid Cymru at the devolved level after the 2021 Senedd election, reflecting changed inter-party and policy dynamics under devolution.[d68245236s1p0]

sub_answers.sub_question: List documented instances in the last 20 years when internal Welsh Labour factions or leadership contenders clashed: provide dates, names (e.g., specific AMs/MSs, shadow ministers, constituency figures), the issues at stake (policy, candidate selection, ideology), procedural moves (no-confidence motions, resignations, leadership challenges) and authoritative sources reporting each event.
sub_answers.text: Carwyn Jones resigned as party leader and First Minister on 21 April 2018, triggering a Welsh Labour leadership contest that attracted multiple nominations and internal contestation [d33580665s5p0].  Mark Drakeford declared his candidacy two days later and immediately secured the public support of seven other Labour AMs, and later a majority of the Labour Group, illustrating factional alignments during the contest [d33580665s5p0].  A rule change to a variation of one member, one vote for Welsh Labour leadership elections was decided at a special conference on 15 September 2018 amid leadership-bid dynamics and campaigning for electoral reform within the party [d33580665s5p0].  In 2024 Darren Millar tabled a non-binding motion of no confidence in First Minister Vaughan Gething over donations made during the 2024 Welsh Labour leadership election and the sacking of former Social Partnership Minister Hannah Blythyn; the motion passed 29–27 but Gething said he would remain as First Minister [d10104837s9p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Provide concrete examples of conflicts in Welsh Labour involving trade unions, local party members, and parliamentary representatives: include disputes over union influence on candidate selection or party policy, financial or affiliation controversies, recorded disagreements between MPs/MSs and affiliated unions, and documented outcomes (discipline, policy reversals, selection result) with sources.
sub_answers.text: Welsh Labour leadership candidates can be nominated via three nominations from affiliated organisations that must include at least two affiliated trade unions, creating formal roles for unions in candidate selection procedures [d83134346s1p0].  During his 2018 leadership campaign, Mark Drakeford received support from eight trade unions and 24 Constituency Labour Parties, demonstrating direct trade-union involvement in leadership contests [d33580665s5p0].  The party’s nomination thresholds require combinations of Senedd group support and CLP or affiliated organisation nominations, institutionalizing potential points of dispute between local party members, unions and parliamentary representatives over who qualifies to stand [d83134346s1p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Summarise criticisms from political commentators, activists, or rival parties about Welsh Labour's approach to Welsh national identity and its relationship with Plaid Cymru: cite specific episodes (e.g., debates over bilingualism, devolution powers, cooperation agreements, responses to Plaid policy proposals), who made the criticisms, and what concrete policy or strategic limitations were highlighted.
sub_answers.text: Welsh Labour entered a co-operation agreement with Plaid Cymru following the 2021 Senedd election, indicating a tactical relationship between the two parties on devolved governance [d53343s0p0].  Plaid Cymru has campaigned for Welsh independence and positions itself as a centre-left to left-wing Welsh nationalist alternative, creating an ideological challenge to Labour on Welsh national identity and devolution policy [d53343s0p0].  Plaid were junior coalition partners with Welsh Labour between 2007 and 2011, showing prior instances of institutional partnership and tension around shared governance arrangements [d53343s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Identify electoral and structural pressures that could erode Welsh Labour’s long-term dominance: compile evidence such as recent vote-share trends by region and demographic (age, language, urban/rural), effects of the Additional Member System/PR on seat conversion, impact of boundary or mandate changes, growth of rival parties (Plaid Cymru, Conservatives, Greens), and turnout patterns that favor opponents—include dates and statistical sources.
sub_answers.text: The Senedd Cymru (Members and Elections) Act 2024 changed the Welsh voting system to closed-list proportional representation using the D’Hondt method with 16 larger constituencies electing six MSs each, starting with the 2026 election, altering the electoral mechanics that previously advantaged Labour under the former Additional Member System [d238480s9p0][d74854646s4p0].  The 2024 Act reduced the number of Senedd constituencies and mandated six-member closed-list seats, and these boundary and system changes were implemented for the 2026 Senedd election [d74854646s4p0][d79435565s1p0].  Plaid Cymru won a plurality in the 2026 Senedd election with 43 out of 96 seats, demonstrating electoral growth by a major rival under the new system and creating pressure on Labour’s dominance [d53343s0p0].  Parliamentary voting on the reform bill saw the entire Conservative Party oppose it while every other party supported it, indicating cross-party shifts in structural rules that can reshape party fortunes [d74854646s4p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: List the key policy commitments Welsh Labour highlighted in its most recent Senedd election manifestos and policy documents, broken down by sector (NHS and social care, schools and FE, housing, economy and jobs, climate and transport) and noting specific targets, funding promises, or legislative proposals and the manifesto year(s).
sub_answers.text: In the NHS and social care sector Welsh Labour's 2021 manifesto included schemes to invest in mental health services, to create a new medical school in North Wales, and to move towards free-at-point-of-use social care ideally as part of UK-wide reform (2021) [d33580665s8p0]. In schools and further education the 2021 manifesto proposed tutoring staff to help pupils catch up after the pandemic, funding to improve school facilities, increasing eligibility for free school meals, expanding access to Welsh-medium education, and potential reform to the school routine (2021) [d33580665s8p0]. In housing the 2021 manifesto included plans for more social housing and associated funding promises (2021) [d33580665s8p0]. In economy and jobs the 2021 manifesto committed to schemes linked to education recovery and a new medical school to boost regional skills and employment (2021) [d33580665s8p0]. In climate and transport the 2021 manifesto included promises for more reforestation and signalled possible transport-related reforms tied to wider policy aims (2021) [d33580665s8p0].

sub_answers.text: The Senedd has powers to legislate devolved taxes, set Welsh income tax rates, and give Welsh Ministers borrowing powers for capital spending, which enabled Welsh Labour administrations to pursue fiscal and spending decisions distinct from UK-wide Westminster legislation (statutory framework from Wales Act 2014 and subsequent devolution arrangements) [d69956499s15p0]. Lynne Neagle, a Welsh Labour MS, criticized the Morgan government over health policy for lacking targets and criticized the elimination of school league tables, indicating intra-party divergence over health and education policy implementation in Wales (first and second Senedd periods up to 2007) [d11203126s2p0]. sub_answers.sub_question: Since the creation of the Senedd, what documented changes have been made to Welsh Labour’s internal decision-making and policy processes—such as new policy committees, devolution of policy authority from UK HQ, separate Welsh manifestos, budgeting and staffing for Welsh policy teams, procedures for resolving conflicts between UK and Welsh policy positions, and case studies of policy divergence?
sub_answers.text:
The 2026 Senedd election was the first following institutional reforms that increased the Senedd from 60 to 96 members, adopted party-list proportional representation and reduced the term from five to four years [d68245236s0p0].
Welsh Labour lost government and its status as the largest party for the first time since devolution began in 1999 in the 2026 election, producing historic realignment in Welsh politics [d68245236s0p0].
Welsh Labour leadership changed multiple times between 2023 and 2026 with leaders standing down and new leaders elected, including an uncontested Welsh Labour leadership election in July 2024 and the appointment of Ken Skates as interim leader on 9 May 2026 [d68245236s1p0][d83134346s0p0].
